Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-09-09 | AAPL | Overweight | +5.4% | +6.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Build AAPL toward a standard 5.0% weight, but initiate at 2.0% of portfolio at market (~$315.34) rather than the trader's 2.5%, because the plan's stop language as written leaves the starter exposed to $284.35, not $300. Fix that first: make $300 a hard closing-basis stop on the entire position (~2.0x the $7.63 ATR, coincident with the July 31 low $300.00 and the lower Bollinger band at $299.82), capping total risk on the starter near 10bps of portfolio. Then earn the rest: +1.0% on an orderly dip into $310-$312 that does not close below $309.90, +1.0% only on a close above $320.28 on >50M shares (4.0% cap before the print), and the final 1.0% only after the late-October FQ4 confirms gross margin >=49% and inventory conversion. $309.90 is an adds-off switch, not an exit; a close below the rising 200-SMA at $284.35 is the strategic invalidation. Horizon 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the FQ4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not the contested question - the stop mechanics and the event clock are, and both were won by the conservative and neutral seats on points the aggressive seat never answered with arithmetic.

What the aggressive seat won outright: the operating record. 9M FY26 revenue +16.2% to $364.4B, Q3 revenue +16.4%, gross profit +25.3%, operating income +26.6%, diluted EPS +28.7%, nine-month EPS +22.4% to $6.88 despite a 219bp tax headwind, Q3 gross margin 50.06%, $110.2B of nine-month FCF (+52.5%, 115.3% cash conversion), $62.2B net cash, debt down 14.5%, no new long-term issuance. The conservative seat conceded the franchise and never dented it. The primary trend reads the same way: price is +10.9% above a rising 200-SMA at $284.35, 7.28% off its record close, +16.36% YTD, and the MACD line at +1.799 is still above its signal at +1.374, so the August 26 crossover is technically alive. That is why this is not Hold and not Underweight - my own log shows what under-owning an intact primary trend in this name costs (08-17, 08-20, 08-21, the July Underweights, and the 08-25 Hold that forfeited +5.5% of five-day alpha).

Where the aggressive seat lost, decisively, three times. First, the stop: the plan says "close below $300 cut to 2.5%," which is a no-op if you start at 2.5%, so the initial tranche's only exit is $284.35 - roughly 9.8% below spot, about 24.5bps of portfolio risk, not the "12 basis points" claimed. The conservative seat caught it and the neutral seat formalized it; the aggressive seat never repaired it, only restated the number. I fix it by making $300 a hard closing stop on the whole tranche at 2.0% size (~10bps risk).

Second, the event clock: the aggressive seat kept framing the September 9 launch (foldable iPhone, iPhone 18, enhanced Siri, Ternus, the ~$2,400 premium foldable) as an unspent catalyst, but the data is as of the 2026-09-09 close and that tape IS the post-event tape - failed from $319.15, closed $315.34 in the lower half of the range on 65.64M shares (~1.6x normal), below the 50-SMA ($316.47), the 10-EMA ($318.26) and the VWMA ($317.04). That may be macro risk-off as much as event disappointment, but the launch is no longer free optionality. The news set is also preview/summary-only with no Apple confirmation, no preorder data and no reviews, so the event cannot be underwritten in either direction.

Third, both payoff framings overstate. The aggressive 1.2:1 to the $333.43 gap and 1.6:1 to the ~$340 record is acceptable, not compelling; the conservative 9.8% down versus 4.1% up to the $328.30 upper band is unfair because it measures downside to deep strategic support while capping upside at near-term resistance. The neutral read - the base case is chop in the $309.90-$328.30 box and we are mid-box - is the honest one.

Where the conservative seat overreached: its menu of a volume-confirmed $320.28 reclaim or a flush to $300-$305 before any exposure turns staged accumulation into momentum chasing and, with a $7.63 ATR, invites a worse fill or none. That is precisely the error my reflection log records repeatedly (08-19, 08-26: gate 1-3% below a rising tape, never fills; take the ATR-sized starter near spot and put the caution in size). It also treats the inventory build ($11.1B, raw materials +260%, days-on-hand ~10.3 to ~18.5) and the ~$13B intangible matched by a ~$13.5B noncurrent liability as a veto rather than a gate - the aggressive seat is right that a pre-launch raw-material build is what a fall cycle looks like before conversion. But the conservative seat is right that if it fails to convert, the 50.06% gross margin carrying the whole margin story is the first casualty, and that a 15.39% to 17.58% tax-rate climb plus a 12% decline in buybacks ($62.1B) remove part of the EPS slope.

So the neutral construction carries the day with the conservative arithmetic bolted on: a smaller, hard-stopped starter, adds reserved for support stabilization or volume-confirmed strength, and the Q4 print as the final gate. Underweight is wrong because trend, franchise and cash generation are intact. Buy at the trader's full 2.5% on a stop that isn't really there is wrong because the post-event distribution day, VWMA overhead at $317.04 and MACD histogram collapse (+2.028 on 9/3 to +0.426 on 9/9) make mid-box a poor place for full size.

What would change the call: upgrade toward Buy on a close above $320.28 on >50M shares with the histogram re-expanding and acceptance above $333.43, or on an FQ4 print with gross margin >=49%, inventory flat-to-down and the intangible footnote explained. Downgrade to Underweight on a close below $300, on FQ4 gross margin below 48% with decelerating revenue, on any inventory write-down, or on a close below the 200-SMA at $284.35. Stated gaps: no P/E or EV/FCF was supplied by either side, so "premium multiple is justified" is unsupported and the 34.9x figure is unverified; no options chain or implied-vol data, so the protective put/collar into the Q4 print cannot be priced here; no segment or geographic mix, so gross-margin durability is unattributable; the $13B intangible has no footnote, which is why net cash flexibility is treated as overstated and the starter stays half-size; and with no portfolio context, all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight and every cited level is technical rather than valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 328.3

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day +6.5% alpha (raw +5.4%) confirms the Overweight directional call, but five days cannot validate a thesis explicitly keyed to the late-October FQ4 print, so treat this as a favorable draw, not proof. It supports the part of the thesis that mattered most — refusing to under-own an intact primary trend, and taking the ATR-sized 2.0% starter at $315.34 instead of waiting for the conservative seat's flush to $300-$305 or a volume-confirmed $320.28 reclaim, a gate that would have forfeited most of this move. It undercuts the "mid-box chop in the $309.90-$328.30 box" base case and the read of the 9/9 distribution day as genuine overhead, since $317.04 VWMA resistance did not hold. Lesson: write adds as ATR-scaled tranches with a time-based fallback, not as price gates below a rising tape — gated adds at $310-$312 are the same non-fill error already logged on 08-19 and 08-26.

[2026-09-08 | AAPL | Underweight | +4.8% | +5.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL — reduce, don't exit, and do it into strength. Trim to roughly 45% of a standard full AAPL allocation before the 9/9 event (40–50% band; 50–60% only if the account passes a strict gap stress), working the balance out on any push into $318.91 (10-EMA) to $320.70 (9/8 high), and finishing at market by 9/9 if no bounce appears. Size the residual so an −8% launch gap costs no more than 0.5% of portfolio — the trader's −5% test is too loose given AAPL gapped −6.12% (6/25) and −7.35% on 132.5M shares (7/31) this quarter, and the 314.90 "stop" is only 0.18 ATR in a 7.51-point-ATR name, i.e. a tripwire, not protection. Do not short AAPL at $316.22 and do not rebuild to 70–75% on a pre-event close above $320.70; post-event ladder: >$320.70 → 55–60%, >$328–331 on multiple closes with a held retest → 70–75%, full weight only on a sustained breakout above $331 on >1.2× volume plus a retest, or Q4 confirmation of gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory converting. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the 9/9 launch and the late-October FQ4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not the contested question in this debate — all three risk seats, the Research Manager, and the trader converge on reducing AAPL. Only the size and the rebuild geometry are genuinely disputed, and that is where I rule.

What is established and undisputed. AAPL is a 16% grower at 50.06% gross margin (+357bp), diluted EPS +28.7%, $110.2B of nine-month FCF, $62.22B net cash, debt/equity 0.78×, price 11.3% above a rising 200-SMA at $284.11 with an unbroken higher-low sequence (246.00 → 273.75 → 300.00 → 302.94 → 314.90). The conservative analyst conceded the franchise; nobody rebutted it. That is why this is not a Sell and why shorting is wrong — the aggressive and conservative seats both rejected a short at $316.22, and the ATR (7.51 points, 2.37%) plus the corporate bid at $315–330 make a short as badly-geometried as the long it would replace.

Why the reduction still wins. First, valuation. The plan's own base case of $334–$366 is FY27E math; on FY26E, 32–35× × ~$8.95 is $286–$313, i.e. spot at or above the top of the band, against a report bear case of −20% to −29%. Reaching the bull target requires two stacked assumptions (FY27 EPS of $10.45 and the market still paying 32–35× it). Second, the tape is decaying at the exact moment of a dated catalyst: two closes below the 10-EMA ($318.91) and below the VWMA ($317.14), price only $0.42 above a 50-SMA that rises 0.4–0.7 points a session, MACD histogram contracting 2.028 → 1.558 → 0.934 with a projected bearish crossover ~9/10–9/12, RSI collapsing 63.38 → 50.20 in three sessions, a 9/3 upper-band overshoot and rejection at the 328.21–330.81 gap-fill ceiling, and a lower high of 344.57 → 330.81. Third, fundamental deceleration on the plan's own numbers: Q4 FY26 modeled at +8–11% versus Q3's +16.4% (the 9/9 launch ships into FY27 Q1), a 219bp tax headwind (17.58% vs 15.39%), R&D +32.5% for 115bp of expense ratio against $13.3B of new intangibles with a 12–24 month monetization window, and inventory days doubling to 18.5. Fourth, and the strongest single point in the debate, earnings quality: roughly $25B of the $35B OCF increase came from other-operating-liability swings plus a $10.8B cash-tax benefit, with the report itself modelling FY27 OCF at low-to-mid teens. The bull cited that flattered number as structural, which is an error, not a debating tactic.

Where each seat wins and loses. The aggressive seat is right that holding full size into a dated binary with a four-point ceiling and a five-point floor is not conservatism, and right that the rebuild ladder is what makes the trim cheap to reverse. He is wrong that 50–60% plus a 1.32-point stop is "convexity" — the neutral's arithmetic is decisive: a 50–60% residual whose −5% gap costs 0.5% of portfolio implies a −10% gap costs ~1.0%, and 320.70 is the 9/8 high, still below the 328–331 rejection zone, so restoring 70–75% on a pre-event close there is adding into the binary, not de-risking. The conservative seat wins on gap realism (stops do not stop gaps; 9/4 ranged 11.07 points, 1.45 ATR) and on refusing a one-close, 1.2×-volume full restore when 7/31 proved a 132.5M-share spike can be distribution — but overreaches in cutting to 25–35% and demanding multiple closes, a retest and fundamental confirmation before re-engaging 70–75% on a name with a rising 200-SMA and $62.2B of net cash. The neutral seat's construction carries: 40–50% residual, a −8% gap stress to 0.5% of portfolio, no pre-event rebuild, staged post-event confirmation.

Why not Hold — the prior-lesson problem, addressed head-on. My own record is emphatic that AAPL Underweights inside an intact uptrend have cost alpha repeatedly: +2.7% (08-17), −0.1% (08-20), +2.9% (08-21), +4.3% (08-27), +0.1% (08-28), −3.9% (08-13), −3.2% to −3.8% (07-20–07-24), while the 08-26 Overweight (+3.7%) and 08-25 Hold (+4.9%) paid. I am not ignoring that; I am refusing to let it neutralize a decision the evidence supports, because this setup is the inverse of those failures. Those trims were made at triple-tested support on momentum decay alone, with nothing but a sub-1% falsification gate. Here I am trimming at or above the top of the base-case valuation band, into rejected supply at 328–331, with MACD, RSI, 10-EMA and VWMA all already broken, one day before a dated binary, and with a written rebuild ladder. Three mitigations carry the lesson forward: keep a real core (40–50%, not the conservative's 25–35%), stagger trims into strength at 318.91–320.70 rather than dumping into weakness, and pre-commit the rebuild levels so the trim is cheap to reverse rather than a directional bear bet. Five-day alpha on a 1–3 month call is noise; the triggers are the scorecard.

What would change the rating. Upgrade to Hold/Overweight on a close above $331.00 resolving the 328.21–330.81 ceiling on >1.2× 20-session volume and holding a retest (first restoring to 70–75%), or on the Q4 FY26 print showing gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory converting rather than writing down, Q4 revenue growth ≥+8%, and FY27 OCF growth in the low-to-mid teens. Downgrade toward Sell on a close below $300.00 breaking the March-to-September higher-low structure (token 10–15% residual, next reference $284.11, ~−10%), on gross margin below 48% with revenue decelerating, on an inventory write-down, or on simultect departures in services or silicon leadership accompanying the Ternus/Cook transition.

Stated gaps I could not resolve from this debate, and which the caller should fill before upgrading: the content of the KeyBanc note (both sides argued about a headline), the specific terms of the CEO transition announcement, FY27 consensus EPS, any multiple comparison versus mega-cap peers, and any options chain or implied-vol data (so the proposed $328–$331 call-spread overlay cannot be priced here, and simple reduction is the more reliable control). There is no portfolio context supplied, so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation and every cited level is technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 305.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the 9/9 launch and the late-October FQ4 FY26 print

REFLECTION:
The +5.9% five-day alpha (raw +4.8%) shows the Underweight directional call was wrong in this window, though five days is too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis tied to the 9/9 launch and FQ4. It undercuts the tape-decay and dated-catalyst legs—trimming into strength at $318.91–$320.70 missed the move—and reinforces the logged pattern that AAPL Underweights inside an intact higher-low uptrend cost alpha, while the valuation-ceiling and earnings-quality concerns remain untested. Next time, require a confirmed trigger—a close below the 10-EMA/50-SMA or post-event rejection—before cutting core exposure in an intact uptrend, and express caution through gap-sized residual and the rebuild ladder rather than pre-event de-risking.
